docs.title: Install Paprika and deploy your first Application
docs.description: Set up the Paprika CLI and Kubernetes operator, create an Application, and inspect its first Release and workload health.

image.alt: An Application pins a Git revision, optionally runs a Pipeline, creates a Release and applies resources to a Kubernetes target.
image.caption: The first Application connects source configuration to a Release and live Kubernetes resources. Pipeline work is optional; the Stage selects the target.

docs.title: Paprika concepts and feature guide
docs.description: Understand Applications, Templates, Pipelines, Stages and Releases, then find the guide for your delivery or observability task.

image.alt: Application, optional Pipeline, Release and Kubernetes resources connected by delivery and observation arrows.
image.caption: Applications describe intent, Releases pin source identity, and Paprika observes resource health and desired/live synchronization.

docs.title: Paprika CLI reference
docs.description: Install and authenticate the Paprika command-line client, inspect applications and releases, and work with delivery controls.

image.alt: The Paprika CLI sends an authenticated request to the API, which checks permissions and works with Kubernetes resource records.
image.caption: CLI commands use the Paprika API. Read the resulting resource state to distinguish an accepted action from a completed rollout.

docs.title: Run Kubernetes delivery pipelines
docs.description: Configure container steps, dependencies, concurrency, retries and declared artifacts in Paprika Pipelines backed by Kubernetes Jobs.

image.alt: A build step branches into unit and policy tests; the package step waits for both prerequisites.
image.caption: Illustrative Pipeline: container Jobs follow declared dependencies, with at most two steps running in parallel. Outputs are explicit references.

docs.title: Promote releases through dev, staging and production
docs.description: Connect environment-specific Applications with pinned Git revisions, upstream verification, candidate approval and explicit target settings.

image.alt: Separate dev, staging and production Applications select environment targets while verification and approval gate a pinned Git revision.
image.caption: Illustrative promotion: each environment has its own Application and target settings. Production retains its accepted Release while a candidate awaits approval.

docs.title: Configure canary deployments
docs.description: Set canary steps and intervals, connect traffic routing, inspect rollout progress, and configure analysis for Kubernetes releases.

image.alt: Canary configuration routes traffic between stable and candidate backends, with workload, interval and analysis gates before each advance.
image.caption: Example weights of 10, 25, 50 and 100 percent illustrate a configured rollout, not live traffic. Workload convergence and configured analysis gate each step.

docs.title: Inspect Kubernetes drift and pruning
docs.description: Compare desired manifests with live resources, understand sync classifications, preview stale resources, and configure opt-in pruning.

image.alt: Desired replicas are three while the live Deployment has two ready replicas; sync comparison and workload health are separate observations.
image.caption: Illustrative resource comparison: two ready replicas can be healthy while still differing from the desired count of three. Review prune candidates separately.

docs.title: Manage delivery across Kubernetes clusters
docs.description: Register deployment targets, configure direct or satellite connections, and understand cluster inventory and application placement.

image.alt: A Stage selects a registered Cluster and its in-cluster, direct or agent connection before applying resources to the target.
image.caption: Cluster registration and deployment transport determine where a Stage applies resources. Satellite observation alone does not prove that deployment access works.

docs.title: Connect the observability gateway
docs.description: Configure Paprika Observe providers and authenticated MCP access for querying metrics, logs, traces and saved dashboards.

image.alt: An authenticated MCP client queries the Observe gateway, which authorizes bounded reads against metrics, logs and traces providers.
image.caption: The separate /observe/mcp surface connects authorized clients to telemetry providers. Inspect freshness and query results as well as provider reachability.

docs.title: Use dashboard examples with real data
docs.description: Explore Paprika Insights examples, map their queries to connected providers, and inspect live results without a sample-data fallback.

image.alt: Discover real provider IDs, bind saved queries and parameters to dashboard widgets, then verify data and layout.
image.caption: Adapt examples by binding their queries to actual providers. Execute the saved dashboard and inspect returned data before relying on its panels.

docs.title: Monitor Paprika metrics and alerts
docs.description: Read controller, drift, prune and delivery metrics, configure Prometheus scraping, and adapt alert rules to your installation.

image.alt: Paprika exposes instrumentation at /metrics for Prometheus to scrape and evaluate with queries and alert rules.
image.caption: Metrics become useful after scraping, label selection and freshness checks. Tune alert thresholds and durations to the installation.

docs.title: Render dashboards for visual verification
docs.description: Deploy the optional private browser worker and inspect saved dashboards at different viewport sizes without replacing live data checks.

image.alt: Authorized dashboard identity and ETag pass to a private browser worker, which returns a real Insights screenshot for visual inspection.
image.caption: The optional worker captures the actual Insights interface at the requested viewport. Use query_dashboard alongside the image to verify data freshness and errors.

docs.title: Connect an MCP client to Paprika
docs.description: Configure Codex, Claude Code or another MCP client for your Paprika server and complete the native OAuth sign-in flow.

image.alt: Configure an MCP client, complete native OAuth, then verify authorized fleet or Observe tools on the selected endpoint.
image.caption: Choose /mcp for fleet operations or /observe/mcp for telemetry. Their audiences and permissions are separate; client setup does not grant server access.

docs.title: Use the Paprika fleet plugin
docs.description: Install the Paprika plugin for Codex or Claude, inspect fleet and application state, and understand permissions for delivery actions.

image.alt: A plugin configures the client connection, OAuth grants approved access, and tool discovery verifies the selected Paprika surface.
image.caption: The plugin supplies client configuration and guidance. Sign in to the intended server and verify available tools before using delivery actions.

docs.title: Install and use Paprika Observe
docs.description: Install the Observe plugin, connect with OAuth, discover telemetry providers, and create or update shared Insights dashboards.

image.alt: Provider discovery leads to saved queries and dashboard widgets, followed by execution and visual verification.
image.caption: After connecting Observe, discover genuine provider IDs and reuse or create queries. Editing a shared dashboard requires the exact ETag and appropriate write access.

docs.title: Paprika API reference
docs.description: Explore Paprika's Connect-RPC API for applications, releases, pipelines and related resources, with request and response examples.

image.alt: A Connect-RPC client sends a request to Paprika, which authenticates and authorizes access to Applications, Releases and related resources.
image.caption: Connect JSON requests and the CLI use the same resource model. Check the response and resulting resource state after an action.

posts.title: Kubernetes health and drift answer different questions
posts.description: A healthy workload can still differ from Git. Learn how to read Kubernetes health, desired-state drift and prune candidates together.

image.alt: A desired Deployment requests three replicas while two live replicas are ready, illustrating healthy workloads that are still out of sync.
image.caption: Illustrative evidence: workload health and desired-state drift answer different questions. A healthy running resource can still differ from Git.

cover.alt: Technical artwork contrasting two healthy running pods with three replicas declared in Git, illustrating the difference between availability and drift.
cover.caption: An illustrative workload can be available while the live configuration still differs from its source of truth.

posts.title: Promoting a tested Git revision across Kubernetes environments
posts.description: Follow one Git revision from dev to production while keeping environment configuration, verification and release approval explicit.

image.alt: Dev and staging verify a pinned revision while production keeps its accepted Release until the separate candidate is approved.
image.caption: Illustrative promotion binds a candidate to a Git revision and verification evidence. Each Application retains its own target configuration and release history.

cover.alt: A pinned revision moves through development and verified staging, while a production candidate waits for approval.
cover.caption: A revision can carry verification evidence forward without overwriting the current production release before approval.

posts.title: Build and verify observability dashboards through MCP
posts.description: Discover real providers, create reusable queries, save dashboards with exact ETags, and verify both live data and the rendered result.

image.alt: Discover real telemetry, bind provider-backed queries to widgets with exact ETags, and verify query execution and the rendered dashboard.
image.caption: MCP dashboard authoring follows discovery, query, save, read-back and verification. A successful save alone does not establish fresh data or a readable layout.

cover.alt: Telemetry from metrics, logs and traces flows through MCP discovery and queries into a verified dashboard.
cover.caption: Discover real providers, run queries, save and read back the document, then inspect its rendered dashboard.

posts.title: Kubernetes release dashboards: the signals that matter before and after a rollout
posts.description: Choose useful Kubernetes release dashboard signals: revision identity, workload health, desired-state drift, Prometheus metrics and evidence freshness.

image.alt: Paprika exposes instrumentation at /metrics for Prometheus to scrape and evaluate with queries and alert rules.
image.caption: Metrics become useful after scraping, label selection and freshness checks. Tune alert thresholds and durations to the installation.

cover.alt: An illustrated release evidence board connects source revision, workload readiness, drift comparison and provider-backed service signals.
cover.caption: A reliable rollout view keeps source identity, health, drift and service telemetry distinct.

posts.title: Prometheus dashboard query patterns: rates, gauges and histograms
posts.description: Write defensible PromQL for dashboards: distinguish counters, gauges, histograms, labels, missing data and aggregation before building charts.

image.alt: Paprika exposes instrumentation at /metrics for Prometheus to scrape and evaluate with queries and alert rules.
image.caption: Metrics become useful after scraping, label selection and freshness checks. Tune alert thresholds and durations to the installation.

cover.alt: Three technical chart panels distinguish a counter and rate, a gauge and histogram bucket distributions.
cover.caption: Prometheus query semantics determine what a panel can truthfully report; visuals come afterward.

posts.title: Observability dashboard design: layout, charts and readable KPIs
posts.description: Design useful observability dashboards with clear KPI hierarchy, chart selection, responsive layouts, accessible tooltips and visible missing-data states.

image.alt: Discover real provider IDs, bind saved queries and parameters to dashboard widgets, then verify data and layout.
image.caption: Adapt examples by binding their queries to actual providers. Execute the saved dashboard and inspect returned data before relying on its panels.

cover.alt: A structured observability dashboard mockup shows primary KPIs, a time-series diagnostic view and a distribution with explicit labels.
cover.caption: Decision-first composition places exceptions, trends and context where operators can find them.

posts.title: Visual testing for observability dashboards: data, layout and MCP verification
posts.description: Test saved dashboards beyond JSON validation: verify queries, revisions, desktop and mobile charts, tooltip bounds and empty states.

image.alt: Authorized dashboard identity and ETag pass to a private browser worker, which returns a real Insights screenshot for visual inspection.
image.caption: The optional worker captures the actual Insights interface at the requested viewport. Use query_dashboard alongside the image to verify data freshness and errors.

cover.alt: Desktop and phone dashboard screens show validation of KPI cards, tooltips, missing data and responsive layout.
cover.caption: Data verification and actual browser inspection are separate acceptance checks for every dashboard.
